title: Midwest ownership, build stages and transaction watch
lede: Prioritize owner-verified commercial routes with Joink, Metro, Midwest Fiber Networks, WIN Technology and selected Iowa, Missouri and Kentucky operators. Keep recent consolidators, cooperatives and public-company platforms in separate lanes, and do not count announced acquisitions as closed.
scope: Public-source review as of September 20, 2026. The operator screen covers Illinois and Indiana plus selected Wisconsin, Iowa, Missouri, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio and Kansas platform cases. County names identify public footprint or project clusters, not route connections, physical diversity, enterprise availability or seller willingness. Scale is stated only with its source date and unit. No new FCC availability counts are calculated or presented. Iowa and Kentucky contain selected named cases from a targeted ten-case review, not exhaustive full-state shortlists. Commercial priorities and countercases are analytical judgments.

sections.title: Start with four commercially distinct lanes
paragraphs: Rightfiber completed the Ritter and Great Plains Communications combination on September 2, 2026. Legacy GPC already includes InterCarrier Networks and Enhanced Telecommunications Corporation. The announced $1.6 billion credit facility is not evidence of undrawn acquisition cash. The next screen should therefore pay only for incremental customers, routes or rights. [MW01] [MW02] [MW03]

A shared sponsor is an introduction path, not a legal combination. Grain's majority investment in 123NET closed in July 2024, but 123NET remains outside Rightfiber. The same rule applies to other sponsor-adjacent platforms. [MW46]

rows: 1. Private control and enterprise fiber
Test Midwest Fiber Networks, Joink and Metro for exact endpoint access, reciprocal enterprise coverage and a current owner-level perimeter before discussing control. [MW05] [MW09] [MW32] [MW33]
No usable route or customer adjacency, unavailable rights, secured-asset restrictions, sponsor resistance or economics that are cheaper through a wholesale contract.
2. Wholesale and middle mile
Price WIN, Bluebird and 123NET capacity or dark fiber at named endpoints. Require route, title, IRU, restoration and assignment schedules. [MW28] [MW41] [MW42] [MW47] [MW48]
Planned construction is not complete, the physical path shares risk with the existing network, or the operator cannot convey the required rights.
3. Cooperative and municipal-style partnerships
Use joint builds, reciprocal transport and operating partnerships with Adams, Endeavor, WK&T and selected Wisconsin cooperatives. [MW21] [MW23] [MW49] [MW50]
Member benefit, grant obligations, lender or regulatory approvals make the structure uneconomic. Do not assume a conventional sale route.
4. Scaled platforms and recent consolidators
Treat Surf, TDS, Socket/IdeaTek, Glo and other funded platforms as competitors, wholesale partners or capital benchmarks unless a discrete carve-out emerges. [MW11] [MW12] [MW24] [MW35] [MW39]
A whole-company proposal offers no advantage over a contract, or sponsor, customer-book, financing and regulatory perimeters cannot be separated.

sections.title: Eighteen operators, with owner and build stage kept separate
paragraphs: This is a strategic screen, not a claim that any operator is for sale. 'No current sale located' means only that the bounded public sources reviewed here did not identify one. County and city clusters are diligence starting points, not proven interconnections.

columns: Ultimate owner and legal / brand perimeter
Named build stage and dated scale
rows: Joink Holdings / Joink / Computer Techniques (IL, IN): Vigo, Clay, Sullivan, Vermillion, Christian, Montgomery and Sangamon county clusters

The 2022 FCC application proposed DIF CIF 2 US LLC at 66% and J K Business Services LLC at 34%; those figures are not a current cap table. FCC authorization became effective September 11, 2022, and Pinpoint's current roster presents CTI as sold to Joink. Exact closing date and present ownership percentages remain unverified, so CTI is grouped with Joink but not treated as a separately available target. [MW05] [MW64] [MW65] [MW61] [MW62]

Operating footprint. Indiana Connectivity Program awards dated October 16, 2025, February 18, 2026 and July 9, 2026 identify small extensions; awards are not proof of completed service. [MW81] No current consolidated passings, subscribers or route-mile figure was located in the bounded sources.
Priority 1 owner-level combination and commercial case. Countercase: it is already a sponsor-backed rollup, and exact cap table, customer migration and route rights remain open.
Metro Communications / Conxxus (IL, IN, MO): central Illinois, Iroquois County and selected southern Illinois / St. Louis-area assets

The January 2026 FCC record identified Zachary Horn with 97.5% equity and 100% voting control of MCC Network Services. MTCO closed into Metro effective January 2, 2026. Only specified Clearwave assets transferred; Clearwave's full national platform did not. [MW06] [MW07] [MW08]

Clifton, Iroquois County was a $610,000 announced fiber investment on February 4, 2026. The FCC authorized the specified Clearwave transfer on March 12. The $459 million financing closed June 23 and comprised $399.2 million of term notes plus a $60 million variable-facility upsize. It included acquired Clearwave assets, supporting acquisition by then, but the exact acquisition date, legal entities and asset schedule still require a closing certificate. [MW09] [MW10]
Priority 1 commercial and asset-rights diligence. Countercase: recent integrations and securitization make a near-term whole-company sale less likely and may constrain transferable assets.
Surf Internet / Surf Air Wireless (IL, IN, MI): northern Illinois, northern Indiana and Michigan

Macquarie Capital led a January 2026 investment alongside Bain Capital and Future Standard. Public sources did not disclose control percentages. Surf Internet is the operating brand; Surf Air Wireless LLC is the FCC legal filer. [MW11] [MW61] [MW62]

The company reported service available to more than 300,000 homes and businesses across the three states on May 26, 2026. That is availability, not subscribers. Its Muncie and Yorktown, Indiana build was announced in May 2025 for more than 21,000 locations, with phased construction into 2026. [MW13] [MW14]

Priority 2 transport, dark-fiber, off-net and enterprise-channel partner. Countercase: a $407 million ABS closed March 4, 2026, comprising $332 million of term notes plus a $75 million variable facility, so collateral and sponsor rights complicate acquisition or carve-out work. [MW12]
NITCO / Northwestern Indiana Telephone Company (IN): Porter, Lake, Jasper and Newton county cluster

The public company history documents predecessor ownership but does not provide a current beneficial-owner table. Municipal operating arrangements in Chesterton and East Chicago are not proven NITCO-owned network assets. A July 2026 secondary report described family succession and a management no-sale position, but the underlying company release was not recovered, so both remain unverified leads. [MW17] [MW66]

Operating mixed FTTH and coax perimeter as of August 25, 2025. Undated company pages variously describe 200 miles of own network, more than 285 installed underground miles, more than 300 fiber miles, more than 8,000 residential customers and 1,200 business customers. These vintages and definitions are not reconciled current FTTP passings or unique owned route miles. [MW18] [MW67]

Priority 2 northwest-Indiana commercial and municipal-contract diligence. Countercase: unresolved ownership, unverified seller posture and potentially non-transferable municipal rights block a clean acquisition thesis.
New Lisbon Telephone / New Lisbon Broadband and Communications (IN): Wayne, Henry and Randolph county cluster

NLBC is a subsidiary of New Lisbon Telephone within New Lisbon Holdings. Beneficial owners and voting percentages were not established. Taylored Systems joined the group in 2021 and is not a separate target. [MW19] [MW20]

Operating local platform with a company-marketed 25-community enquiry list. Fiber, wireless and other services require address-level classification; the list is not a 25-community FTTH completion claim. No dated 2025-2026 public passings, subscriber, build-mile or financing figure was located. [MW68]
Priority 3 east-central Indiana partnership and ownership diligence. Countercase: the regulated and unregulated entity split, technology mix and transfer restrictions are not yet resolved.
Aureon (IA to Chicago): Iowa Falls-Davenport-Chicago segment within the Ellendale-Chicago partner system
Aureon is owned by 112 independent telecom companies. Its member-shareholder structure is distinct from Bluebird and Rightfiber; no connection among those networks is assumed. [MW69]

Aureon describes an approximately 460-mile, six-strand Iowa Falls-to-Chicago segment as built and operated by Aureon. Its May 2026 release announced a 100-terabit partner route, with capacity and delivery milestones stated by the company rather than independently accepted. [MW70] [MW71]

Priority 1 Iowa wavelength, fiber and enterprise-transport diligence. Countercase: member ownership, unknown spare rights and no verified Rightfiber handoff make this a commercial case, not a conventional bolt-on.
Endeavor Communications / Clay County Rural Telephone Cooperative (IN): central and west-central Indiana
Member-owned cooperative. Members elect the board and receive or reinvest capital credits. [MW22] [MW23]
Operating broadband and communications platform. This screen does not state a new footprint count. [MW22] [MW23]
Priority 3 wholesale, joint-build and reciprocal last mile. Countercase: cooperative approvals and member-benefit standards make a control transaction structurally harder.
Midwest Fiber Networks (WI): southeast Wisconsin and Milwaukee enterprise market

Company materials identify Niksa Ivancevic as owner and CEO, but that title does not establish sole ownership or a complete cap table. MWFN markets enterprise and carrier fiber plus an MWFN Home residential FTTH offering; one support FAQ still says it does not serve households, so the current service perimeter is internally inconsistent. [MW32] [MW34] [MW72] [MW73]

The current company map reports more than 5,300 fiber-network miles, accessed September 20, 2026. Residential pages name select areas in Kenosha, Racine, Washington and Ozaukee counties, but activation dates, subscriber split and legal asset perimeter are unknown. [MW33] [MW72] [MW73]
Priority 1 Wisconsin control and dark-fiber diligence. Countercase: cap table, financials, owned-versus-leased fiber, customers and exact route rights are not public.
WIN Technology (WI, IL, IA, MI and broader Midwest): statewide middle mile and northern Illinois

WIN says it is owned by 31 independent Wisconsin telephone companies. Digicorp joined WIN in 2024. The member companies and WIN must not be treated as one freely transferable asset pool. [MW27] [MW29]

WIN reported more than 22,000 network miles across six states on May 15, 2026. The same release described the planned Denver-to-Chicago Heartland Fiber Project as a $700 million, 2,000-mile build, with a summer 2026 construction start and one-to-two-year deployment. Those planned miles are not operating network. [MW28]
Priority 1 wholesale, wavelength, dark-fiber and joint-build case. Countercase: member consent, available rights and completion of the planned Heartland route remain unverified.
TDS Telecom (WI): Walworth, Kenosha, Waukesha and Dane county clusters
Wholly owned by Telephone and Data Systems, Inc., a controlled public company. TDS is a mixed fiber, coax and copper operator, not a pure-fiber target. [MW24]

At June 30, 2026 TDS reported 1.9 million total service addresses and 567,700 residential broadband connections across its full footprint. Southeast Wisconsin construction was announced in October 2025 for roughly 24,000 to 26,000 locations, with the release itself using different headline and body figures. Completion was not established. [MW24] [MW25]

Countercase and competitive benchmark. TDS closed the Granite State acquisition September 1, 2026, but acquisition posture does not prove that every discrete Wisconsin asset is unavailable. No Wisconsin sale process is established. [MW26]
Bug Tussel / Hilbert Communications (WI): Jefferson and Kewaunee county projects

Wisconsin records identify Hilbert Communications doing business as Bug Tussel 1. Current ultimate equity ownership was not verified. Bug Tussel, Red Tail Tower and Spiralight require a current legal-entity bridge. [MW30] [MW31]

The Young Prairie FTTP project remained open as of May 28, 2026 and targeted 131 residential plus 5 business locations. [MW30] A separate March 18, 2021 Kewaunee award proposed a 61.7-mile fiber route to support wireless service; it is not a completed-mileage or FTTH-passings figure. [MW80]

Priority 3 tuck-in or tower/fiber partnership diligence. Countercase: hybrid FWA/FTTH technology, grant obligations and unclear ownership could make the usable fiber perimeter much smaller than the marketed reach.
ImOn Communications, including Danville Telecom (IA): Henry, Des Moines and Lee counties; Burlington, Fort Madison, Mount Pleasant and Keokuk cluster
Goldman Sachs Asset Management's infrastructure business acquired ImOn in April 2022. ImOn later acquired and integrated Danville Telecom, which is not a separate current target. [MW15] [MW16]

For 2025, ImOn reported 532 miles of fiber laid, expansion activity across 17 communities, more than $100 million invested and nine completed projects. These are company statements and do not mean 532 unique route miles or 17 fully built communities. Its March 31, 2026 update described Danville as the southeast-Iowa hub. [MW16]
Priority 2 eastern-Iowa operating and wholesale partner. Countercase: sponsor backing and ongoing expansion make a whole-company transaction less likely than reciprocal access.
Socket / IdeaTek platform (MO, KS and adjacent Midwest): Socket Missouri markets and IdeaTek regional fiber footprint

Oak Hill and Pamlico sponsor the combined platform while Socket and IdeaTek retain separate brands. Fastwyre's Missouri operations closed into Socket on April 30, 2026. Wave Wireless remains outside IdeaTek until its announced acquisition closes. [MW35] [MW36] [MW37]

At platform formation, Socket reported more than 100,000 premises passed. The sponsor set a greater-than-500,000 homes-passed target for 2028. Both are company statements; the latter is a target, not current scale. [MW35]

Priority 2 Missouri commercial partnership and regional platform benchmark. Countercase: recent consolidation, sponsor control and mixed Fastwyre / Wave technologies require a clean brand, customer and asset bridge.
Bluebird Fiber, including acquired Everstream assets (MO and broader Midwest): Jefferson City-Washington, Washington-Rolla, Rolla-Strafford and Springfield-Carthage planned corridors

Macquarie-backed Bluebird announced completion of its Everstream asset and operations purchase on March 6, 2026. Historical disclosures document leased infrastructure, OpCo/PropCo arrangements and Uniti fiber used under long-term IRUs. Current rights must be mapped by span and entity. [MW41] [MW42] [MW43]

NTIA described 325 planned Missouri miles in the 2023 award; the 2024 RFP used 330. The RFP also described planned non-grant connections through Strafford and Springfield. None of those design figures is accepted operating mileage without construction and service-ready evidence. [MW44] [MW45]

Priority 1 Missouri commercial transport and dark-fiber diligence. Countercase: historical rights structures, grant obligations and incomplete as-builts block fee-title, transferable-IRU or carve-out assumptions.
North Central Telephone Cooperative (KY, TN): Allen, Butler, Edmonson, Grayson and Warren county brand footprint

Member-owned cooperative headquartered in Lafayette, Tennessee. Its Kentucky regulated ILEC perimeter and wider brand footprint, including partnership or competitive areas, must remain separate. [MW74]

NCTC reported completing a 100% fiber network of more than 4,300 miles in early 2023. Its Warren RECC model leases dark fiber and sells service over the electric cooperative's FTTH. The 2025 Kentucky filing reported accounting plant additions, not new passings. [MW74] [MW75] [MW76]

Priority 2 Kentucky cooperative partnership and repeatable lease/operating model. Countercase: member and cross-state obligations make a standard control transaction harder than replicating the Warren structure.
Brandenburg Telephone / Brandenburg Telecom (KY): Meade, Hardin and Breckinridge counties plus competitive markets including Elizabethtown
Brandenburg Telephone and Brandenburg Telecom are subsidiaries of Brandenburg Communications Corporation. Ultimate parent shareholders were not disclosed in the reviewed public records. [MW52] [MW53]

The audited 2025 Brandenburg Telephone perimeter reported $13.275 million operating revenue, $7.725 million net income, $85.591 million telephone plant in service and $2.467 million property and equipment purchases. Net income is not EBITDA, and capex is not fiber-only. [MW52]

Priority 3 conventional Kentucky corporate watchlist after route adjacency is proven. Countercase: a profitable regulated group may have no reason to sell, and without a confirmed Rightfiber connection it could be an operating island.
123NET (MI): Southfield-to-Bay City corridor through Oakland, Genesee, Saginaw and Bay-area communities

Grain's majority investment in 123NET closed in July 2024. 123NET remains a separate company from Rightfiber despite common sponsor affiliation. Peninsula Fiber Network is also a separate party to the joint corridor. [MW46]

123NET and PFN announced completion in February 2025 of an approximately 130-mile Southfield-to-Bay City installation. The announcement does not allocate ownership by span or establish Rightfiber access. [MW47] [MW48]
Priority 1 Michigan NNI, wavelength or IRU test. Countercase: no common sponsor shortcut to transfer, no verified GPC interconnection and no public joint-asset schedule.
Glo Fiber / legacy Horizon Telcom / Shentel (OH): Circleville and the acquired Ohio Horizon perimeter

Glo Fiber is a Shentel brand, not a separate owner. Shentel closed the Horizon acquisition April 1, 2024. The Chillicothe Telephone Company is a relevant Ohio operating legal entity; a similarly named Horizon Communications FCC filer in Idaho and Wyoming is unrelated. [MW38] [MW79]

At June 30, 2026 Shentel reported 475,677 Glo expansion passings and 100,155 RGUs, with 728,736 passings and 19,847 fiber route miles company-wide. These units and perimeters are not additive. Circleville upgrades were reported complete August 26, with service available to more than 6,000 homes and businesses. [MW39] [MW40]
Priority 2 Ohio wholesale and competitive benchmark. Countercase: public-company scale and recent integration make a regional bolt-on thesis implausible without a discrete asset carve-out.

sections.title: Keep legal ownership, brands and transaction status straight

rows: InterCarrier Networks versus Indiana Fiber Network

GPC completed InterCarrier Networks in 2019, so it is inside legacy GPC and now Rightfiber. Zayo completed the separately identified Indiana Fiber Network / Intelligent Fiber Network transaction in 2021. [MW02] [MW04]
Do not map the two businesses by the initials ICN or IFN, and do not count either as an independent current target.
Metro and specified Clearwave assets

The FCC authorized the specified transfer March 12, 2026. A June 24 adviser release says acquired Clearwave assets entered collateral for financing closed June 23, supporting acquisition by then. [MW07] [MW09]
Do not assign Clearwave's full footprint to Metro. Exact acquisition closing date, entities, spans, liens and facility connections require the certificate and final asset schedule.
Rightfiber and 123NET
Grain sponsors Rightfiber and separately holds a majority investment in 123NET. [MW01] [MW46]
Common sponsor does not combine legal entities, routes, customers or rights. Use arm's-length terms and verify minority, lender and regulatory consents.
Omni / Lit and Citizens Fiber

Oak Hill was described as majority owner of Omni and Lit when their merger was announced. Omni used completed-acquisition wording for Citizens on June 1, 2026, but a July 11 Pennsylvania Bulletin notice documented pending transfer applications. Closing remains unverified; later July and August docket observations were not independently refreshed in this review. [MW55] [MW57] [MW77] [MW78]
Do not include Citizens inside the confirmed closed Omni perimeter, and do not rely on announcement wording or an unrefreshed docket observation alone.
Socket / IdeaTek and Wave Wireless

Socket and IdeaTek are separate brands in one sponsor platform. Fastwyre Missouri closed into Socket on April 30, 2026. IdeaTek announced Wave Wireless on August 12 with an expected later close. [MW35] [MW36] [MW37]
Do not add Wave locations, customers or assets until closing evidence resolves the legal and technology perimeter.
Eaton Fiber and Ripple Fiber
Bain and Tillman announced Eaton funding and a proposed Ripple acquisition on July 29, 2026. Ripple had separately expanded its own debt capacity in 2025. [MW59] [MW60]
Do not treat the acquisition as closed or combine Ripple financing, locations or network metrics into Eaton without consummation evidence.

sections.title: Twelve dated developments that change the screen

rows: Rightfiber completed the Ritter / GPC combination and announced a $1.6 billion credit facility. [MW01]
The facility is not demonstrated undrawn acquisition cash. Legacy GPC, ICN and ETC must be removed from the target universe.
TDS closed the Granite State acquisition. [MW26]
Reinforces TDS as a scaled strategic buyer and benchmark. It does not establish that a discrete Wisconsin asset is unavailable, and no Wisconsin sale process is established.
Shentel reported Circleville Glo Fiber upgrades complete and service available to more than 6,000 homes and businesses. [MW40]
A completed named Ohio market is more useful than a future build target, but availability is not subscribers.
IdeaTek announced an agreement to acquire Wave Wireless, expected to close later in 2026. [MW37]
Wave remains outside the closed Socket / IdeaTek perimeter until consummation.
Metro closed $459 million of financing; the adviser said acquired Clearwave assets entered the collateral. [MW09]
Supports acquisition by the financing close, while exact transaction date and asset perimeter remain certificate items.
Surf reported service available to more than 300,000 homes and businesses across Illinois, Indiana and Michigan. [MW13]
Confirms regional scale but not fiber subscribers, penetration or a sale process.
WIN and partners announced the Denver-to-Chicago Heartland Fiber Project and reported more than 22,000 WIN network miles across six states. [MW28]
Treat the route as planned until completion and orderability are established.
Socket's purchase of Fastwyre Missouri closed. [MW36]
Move that Missouri perimeter into Socket, but keep other Fastwyre operations and Wave separate.
ImOn reported its 2025 build program and described Danville as its southeast-Iowa hub. [MW16]
Strengthens the commercial Iowa bridge case, while Danville is no longer an independent target.
Bluebird announced completion of the Everstream asset and operations purchase. [MW41]
Completion does not resolve fee title, historical IRUs, assumed contracts or transferable rights by span.
Surf closed a $407 million fiber ABS. [MW12]
Raises the bar for any control or carve-out thesis and makes collateral diligence essential.
Metro announced a $610,000 fiber investment in Clifton, Iroquois County. [MW10]
Provides a named local build, but not a route to a Rightfiber endpoint or completed enterprise connection.

sections.title: Evidence required before advancing a transaction
bullets: Obtain current cap tables, legal-entity charts and beneficial owners. A brand, sponsor relationship or FCC filer name does not define the sale perimeter.
Reconcile closed, announced, approved and operationally transitioning transactions. Citizens, Wave and Ripple remain outside confirmed closed rollups in this review.
Require exact A/Z buildings, route GIS, shared-risk groups, owned versus leased plant, IRUs, easements, grant restrictions, liens and assignment rights. County overlap is not a connection.
Bridge every scale figure by date and unit: passings, serviceable premises, customers, subscribers, RGUs, route miles, awarded projects and completed construction are different measures.

Wisconsin public research identifies credible operators and projects, but the recovered full state FCC source is validated in the separate Wisconsin state model. This model makes no new Wisconsin FCC count.

Iowa and Kentucky rows are the strongest selected cases from a targeted ten-case review, not exhaustive full-state shortlists. Additional cooperative and strategic-counterparty cases remain outside this compact screen.
Only public sources are used. Surf is included only on its public ownership, financing and operating disclosures.
